pairs.subject: usage-pricing-models
pairs.evidence: src/lib/plans.ts:6 Ascent never turns a measured quantity into money: the charge is a fixed-price Polar product (subscription or credit pack), and a metered scan only draws an allowance slot or one integer credit. Searches for graduated, tiersMode, unit_amount and groupingKey across src/ and prisma/ found nothing, so there is no tier ladder, no volume model, no grouping key and no amount arithmetic for this subject to govern.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/plans.ts:415 Prepaid credits are spent per unit, one credit per scan past the allowance. No retroactive (volume) shape exists to refuse, although the technique's shape × timing table is still not written down.
src/lib/plans.ts:183 Ascent stores only a display-only whole-USD mirror. Polar computes and rounds the charged amount, so this context has no rounding boundary of its own.
src/lib/plans.ts:425 The charge decision takes one org-wide month-to-date quantity. No dimension splits it into per-group ladders or allowances.

src/lib/plans.ts:414 The only boundary is a single free-allowance threshold, an exclusive count over integer scans. Plan 'tiers' are entitlement levels, not price ranges, so there are no adjacent ranges whose convention could be inferred.

pairs.subject: usage-pricing-models
pairs.evidence: src/lib/db/usage.ts:150 The dollar figures here are estimates of LLM spend priced from model rate tables, which is the payer's-seat cost-metering discipline this subject excludes. No invoice line or charge is produced, and searches for graduated, tiersMode, unit_amount and groupingKey across the context's directories found nothing.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/db/usage.ts:155 This is an estimate shown on a dashboard and collects no money, which falls under the technique's 'quotes, previews and estimates' exemption.
src/lib/db/usage.ts:259 Lane costs are summed in binary floats. That is acceptable for a payer-side estimate, but it would be a deviation if this figure ever became a charged amount.

src/lib/db/usage.ts:48 Per-repo and per-team breakdowns are reporting over the event stream, not a pricing dimension, and the invoice shape does not change. This is the route the technique prescribes for analytical dimensions.
